description: OWASP NodeGoat (Node.js/Express, MongoDB): every flaw that the in-app tutorial (a1-a10, redos, ssrf) and the source comments document, labeled at its source location.

vulnerabilities.description: handleContributionsUpdate passes req.body.preTax to eval(), which lets an attacker run JavaScript on the server (SSJS injection).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a1.html (A1-1 Server Side JS Injection); comment 'Insecure use of eval() to parse inputs'

vulnerabilities.description: handleContributionsUpdate passes req.body.afterTax to eval() (SSJS injection).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a1.html (A1-1 Server Side JS Injection)

vulnerabilities.description: handleContributionsUpdate passes req.body.roth to eval() (SSJS injection).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a1.html (A1-1 Server Side JS Injection)

vulnerabilities.description: getByUserIdAndThreshold puts the user's threshold query parameter straight into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression, which allows NoSQL/SSJS injection: it can return every user's allocations or cause a DoS with while(true).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a1.html (A1-2 SQL and NoSQL Injection); comment 'Fix for A1 - 2 NoSQL Injection'

vulnerabilities.description: handleLoginRequest logs the raw userName from the request with console.log, so CRLF in the input can forge log entries.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a1.html (A1-3 Log Injection); comment 'Fix for A1 - 3 Log Injection'

vulnerabilities.description: addUser stores the request's password in the users collection as plaintext, not as a salted hash, and validateLogin compares it in plaintext.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a2.html (A2-1 protecting user credentials); comment 'Fix for A2-1 - Broken Auth'

vulnerabilities.description: The express-session config sets no cookie options: no HttpOnly, Secure or maxAge (so the session never times out), and it keeps the default cookie name.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a2.html (A2-1 session timeout and cookies), a3.html (HTTPOnly), a5.html (generic cookie name); comments 'Fix for A3 - XSS' / 'Fix for A5 - Security MisConfig' in the session block

vulnerabilities.description: After a successful login the code sets req.session.userId without calling req.session.regenerate(), which leaves the app open to session fixation and hijacking.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a2.html (A2-1 session hijacking); comment block 'A2-Broken Authentication and Session Management' above it

vulnerabilities.description: validateSignup's password policy /^.{1,20}$/ accepts any password of 1-20 characters, which helps password guessing.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a2.html (A2-2 Password Guessing Attacks); comment 'Fix for A2-2 - Broken Authentication - requires stronger password'

vulnerabilities.description: A failed login for an unknown user returns 'Invalid username', which reveals that the account does not exist (user enumeration).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a2.html (A2-2 username/password enumeration); comment 'Fix for A2-2 Broken Auth - Uses identical error'

vulnerabilities.description: A failed login with a wrong password returns a different message, 'Invalid password', which confirms that the username exists.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a2.html (A2-2 username/password enumeration); comment 'Fix for A2-2 Broken Auth - Uses identical error'

vulnerabilities.description: The swig template engine is configured with autoescape: false, so every {{ }} output in the views renders unescaped.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a3.html (fix: enable autoescape in server.js); comment 'Fix for A3 - XSS, enable auto escaping'

vulnerabilities.description: Stored XSS: the firstName and lastName that a user saves on the profile page are rendered unescaped in the top-right user menu.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a3.html (stored XSS on profile form, shown in top right menu)

vulnerabilities.description: A user-controlled name is put in an href attribute with no URL-context encoding, which allows javascript: links and XSS.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a3.html (output encoding context, profile.js and profile.html); @FIXME comment in profile.html

vulnerabilities.description: doc.website is HTML-encoded but is also used in a URL context, so the wrong encoder leaves XSS possible.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a3.html (output encoding context, profile.js); @TODO @FIXME comment in profile.js

vulnerabilities.description: displayAllocations takes userId from the URL parameter instead of the session, so any logged-in user can view another user's allocations (IDOR).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a4.html (Insecure Direct Object References); comment 'Fix for A4 Insecure DOR'

vulnerabilities.description: GET /benefits is protected only by isLoggedIn, with no isAdmin check, so any user can reach the admin benefits page.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a7.html (Missing Function Level Access Control); comment 'Fix for A7 - checks user role'

vulnerabilities.description: POST /benefits has no isAdmin check, so any logged-in user can change any user's benefit start date.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a7.html (Missing Function Level Access Control)

vulnerabilities.description: No security headers are set: x-powered-by is not disabled, and there is no helmet frameguard/noCache/CSP/HSTS and no nosniff (the fixes are commented out above this spot).
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a5.html (Security Misconfiguration, server.js); comment 'Fix for A5 - Security MisConfig'

vulnerabilities.description: The app listens on plain HTTP (http.createServer), so session cookies and sensitive data travel unencrypted.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a6.html (Sensitive Data Exposure, HTTPS in server.js); comment 'Insecure HTTP connection'

vulnerabilities.description: updateUser stores the user's SSN and date of birth in the database as plaintext, unencrypted.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a6.html (encrypt ssn/dob in data/profile-dao.js); comment 'Fix for A7 - Sensitive Data Exposure - Store encrypted ssn and DOB'

vulnerabilities.description: The csurf middleware is not enabled (it is commented out), so no state-changing POST route (profile, contributions, benefits, memos) checks a CSRF token.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a8.html (CSRF, server.js); comment 'Fix for A8 - CSRF'

vulnerabilities.description: The contributions update form has no _csrf hidden token (it is commented out), so a cross-site request can change contribution percentages.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a8.html; comment 'Fix for A8 - CSRF' in contributions.html

vulnerabilities.description: The /learn route redirects to req.query.url without validating it, which is an open redirect.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial a10.html (Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards); comment 'Insecure way to handle redirects'

vulnerabilities.description: The bankRouting value is checked with /([0-9]+)+\#/, whose nested quantifier backtracks catastrophically on long digit strings and stalls the event loop.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial redos.html; comment 'Fix for Section: ReDoS attack'

vulnerabilities.description: displayResearch joins req.query.url and req.query.symbol and fetches the result server-side with needle.get, so an attacker can make the server request any URL.
vulnerabilities.note: tutorial ssrf.html (Research page, routes/research.js)
